text: And Elihu answered and said,
“Hear, O wise men, my words, and give ear to me, knowing ones.
For the ear shall test words, and the palate tastes to eat.
Let us choose for ourselves what is just; let us know among ourselves what [is] good.
For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, and God has turned aside my justice.
[And] over my justice should I lie? Mortal [is] my arrow, without transgression.’
Who [is] a man like Job, drinking up derision like the water,
and he travels in company with workers of iniquity, and in walking with men of wickedness?
For he has said, ‘Nothing does it profit a man that he should delight in God.’
Therefore, O men of heart, listen to me. Far be it to God from wickedness, and Shaddai from injustice.
For the work of man, he repays to him; and according to the way of a man, He causes him to find [it].
Yes, surely God does not act wickedly, and Shaddai does not pervert justice.
Who gave charge to Him over the earth? And who has set [Him] [over] all of the world?
If He should set His heart to it, gathering His Spirit and His breath to Himself,
[then] all flesh would perish together, and man would return to the dust.
And if [there is] understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.
And shall one hating justice govern? Or will you declare wicked the just and mighty One?
Who says to a king, ‘Worthless,’ [or] to nobles, ‘Wicked’?
Who does not lift the faces of princes, and does not acknowledge the rich before the face of the poor, for they [are] all the work of His hands.
[In] a moment they die, and in the middle of the night the people are shaken and pass away; and the mighty are taken away, not by a hand.
For His eyes [are] upon the ways of man, and all of his steps He sees.
There is no darkness and no shadow of death, [for] the workers of iniquity to be hidden there.
For He does not set upon a man further, for his going before God in the judgment.
He breaks the mighty without investigation, and makes others stand in their place.
Therefore, He recognizes their works, and He overturns [them] in the night, and they are crushed.
In exchange for their wickednesses, He strikes them in a place of seeing,
which [was] upon thus: They turned aside from Him, and they had no regard for any of His ways,
They caused the cry of the poor to cause to come before Him—and He heard the cry of the afflicted.
And he is silent, and who can call Him wicked? And He hides [His] face, and who can see Him? And He is over a nation and over man alike,
from the reigning of godless a man, from the snares of the people.
If one says to God, ‘I have lifted [it], [and] no more will I offend;
besides what I see, You teach me; if I have done iniquity, I will not continue [it]’
will he repay it from with you, because you have rejected [it]? Then you must choose, and not I, and may you speak what you know.
Men of understanding will say to me, and the wise man [who is] listening to me:
‘Job [does] not speak with knowledge, and His words [are] not with wisdom.’
If only Job were tested to the end, upon his answers among men of iniquity!
For he adds rebellion upon his sin; among us he claps, and he multiplies his words against God.”
